sanskrit: āvidhyāvidhya tau vṛkṣān muhūrtam itaretaram tāḍayām āsatur ubhau vinadantau muhur muhuḥ
english: Swinging trees again and again at each other for a while, they both struck blows, roaring repeatedly.

sanskrit: tasmin deśe yadā vṛkṣāḥ sarva eva nipātitāḥ puñjīkṛtāś ca śataśaḥ parasparavadhepsayā
english: When in that place all the trees had been felled and piled in hundreds by those two, each intent on killing the other,

sanskrit: tadā śilāḥ samādāya muhūrtam iva bhārata mahābhrair iva śailendrau yuyudhāte mahābalau
english: then, O Bhārata, they took up rocks and fought for a while, those two mighty ones like great mountains with thunderclouds.

sanskrit: ugrābhir ugrarūpābhir bṛhatībhiḥ parasparam vajrair iva mahāvegair ājaghnatur amarṣaṇau
english: With fierce, terrifying, massive boulders they struck each other like thunderbolts with great force, both filled with fury.

sanskrit: abhihatya ca bhūyas tāv anyonyaṃ baladarpitau bhujābhyāṃ parigṛhyātha cakarṣāte gajāv iva
english: And having struck each other repeatedly, those two proud in strength then grappled with their arms and dragged each other like elephants.

sanskrit: muṣṭibhiś ca mahāghorair anyonyam abhipetatuḥ tayoś caṭacaṭāśabdo babhūva sumahātmanoḥ
english: They fell upon each other with terribly fierce fists, and a crackling sound arose from those two great-souled ones.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃhṛtya muṣṭiṃ tu pañcaśīrṣam ivoragam vegenābhyahanad bhīmo rākṣasasya śirodharām
english: Then drawing back his fist like a five-headed serpent, Bhīma struck the neck of the Rākṣasa with great force.

sanskrit: tataḥ śrāntaṃ tu tad rakṣo bhīmasenabhujāhatam supariśrāntam ālakṣya bhīmaseno 'bhyavartata
english: Then, seeing that Rākṣasa wearied and utterly exhausted from the blows of Bhīmasena's arms, Bhīmasena pressed forward.

sanskrit: tata enaṃ mahābāhur bāhubhyām amaropamaḥ samutkṣipya balād bhīmo niṣpipeṣa mahītale
english: Then mighty-armed Bhīma, equal to an immortal, lifted him up forcibly with both arms and crushed him against the ground.

sanskrit: tasya gātrāṇi sarvāṇi cūrṇayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ aratninā cābhihatya śiraḥ kāyād apāharat
english: The Pāṇḍava crushed all his limbs and, striking him with his elbow, severed the head from the body.

sanskrit: saṃdaṣṭoṣṭhaṃ vivṛttākṣaṃ phalaṃ vṛntād iva cyutam jaṭāsurasya tu śiro bhīmasenabalād dhṛtam papāta rudhirādigdhaṃ saṃdaṣṭadaśanacchadam
english: Jaṭāsura's head, with lips bitten, eyes rolled back, like fruit fallen from its stalk, held by the force of Bhīmasena, fell drenched in blood, with teeth clenching the lips.

sanskrit: taṃ nihatya maheṣvāso yudhiṣṭhiram upāgamat stūyamāno dvijāgryais tair marudbhir iva vāsavaḥ
english: Having slain him, that great archer came to Yudhiṣṭhira, praised by those foremost brahmins, like Vāsava attended by the Maruts.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca nihate rākṣase tasmin punar nārāyaṇāśramam abhyetya rājā kaunteyo nivāsam akarot prabhuḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: With that Rākṣasa slain, King Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, the lord, returned again to the hermitage of Nārāyaṇa and made his abode there.

sanskrit: sa samānīya tān sarvān bhrātṝn ity abravīd vacaḥ draupadyā sahitān kāle saṃsmaran bhrātaraṃ jayam
english: Gathering all his brothers together with Draupadī, he spoke these words in time, remembering his brother Arjuna:

sanskrit: samāś catasro 'bhigatāḥ śivena caratāṃ vane kṛtoddeśaś ca bībhatsuḥ pañcamīm abhitaḥ samām
english: "Four years have passed auspiciously for us dwelling in the forest, and Arjuna has accomplished his purpose — the fifth year is now approaching.

sanskrit: prāpya parvatarājānaṃ śvetaṃ śikhariṇāṃ varam tatrāpi ca kṛtoddeśaḥ samāgamadidṛkṣubhiḥ
english: Having reached Mount Śveta, best of peaks among mountains, there too his purpose was accomplished, and we longed to meet him again.

sanskrit: kṛtaś ca samayas tena pārthenāmitatejasā pañca varṣāṇi vatsyāmi vidyārthīti purā mayi
english: And that Pārtha of boundless splendour made an agreement with me: 'I will dwell five years seeking knowledge,' he said long ago.

sanskrit: tatra gāṇḍīvadhanvānam avāptāstram ariṃdamam devalokād imaṃ lokaṃ drakṣyāmaḥ punarāgatam
english: We shall see the Gāṇḍīva-bowman, subduer of foes, who has obtained all weapons, returning from the world of the gods to this world."

sanskrit: ity uktvā brāhmaṇān sarvān āmantrayata pāṇḍavaḥ kāraṇaṃ caiva tat teṣām ācacakṣe tapasvinām
english: Having spoken thus, the Pāṇḍava took leave of all the brahmins and explained to those ascetics the reason for his departure.

sanskrit: tam ugratapasaḥ prītāḥ kṛtvā pārthaṃ pradakṣiṇam brāhmaṇās te 'nvamodanta śivena kuśalena ca
english: Those brahmins of fierce austerities, pleased, circumambulated Yudhiṣṭhira and blessed him with auspicious words and well-being.

sanskrit: sukhodarkam imaṃ kleśam acirād bharatarṣabha kṣatradharmeṇa dharmajña tīrtvā gāṃ pālayiṣyasi
english: "This hardship, O bull of the Bhāratas, O knower of dharma, will soon bear fruit in happiness; crossing through it by the law of warriors, you shall rule the earth."

sanskrit: tat tu rājā vacas teṣāṃ pratigṛhya tapasvinām pratasthe saha viprais tair bhrātṛbhiś ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: The king, that scorcher of enemies, receiving those words of the ascetics, set out together with those brahmins and his brothers.

sanskrit: draupadyā sahitaḥ śrīmān haiḍimbeyādibhis tathā rākṣasair anuyātaś ca lomaśenābhirakṣitaḥ
english: The glorious one, accompanied by Draupadī, followed by Rākṣasas headed by Ghaṭotkaca, son of Hidimbi, and protected by Lomaśa.

sanskrit: kva cij jagāma padbhyāṃ tu rākṣasair uhyate kva cit tatra tatra mahātejā bhrātṛbhiḥ saha suvrataḥ
english: Somewhere he went on foot, somewhere he was carried by the Rākṣasas — that great-splendoured one of excellent vows, together with his brothers, here and there.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā bahūn kleśān vicintayan siṃhavyāghragajākīrṇām udīcīṃ prayayau diśam
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, reflecting on many hardships, journeyed northward toward the direction filled with lions, tigers, and elephants.

sanskrit: avekṣamāṇaḥ kailāsaṃ mainākaṃ caiva parvatam gandhamādanapādāṃś ca meruṃ cāpi śiloccayam
english: Gazing upon Kailāsa, Mount Maināka, the foothills of Gandhamādana, and Meru the rocky peak,

sanskrit: upary upari śailasya bahvīś ca saritaḥ śivāḥ prasthaṃ himavataḥ puṇyaṃ yayau saptadaśe 'hani
english: ever higher on the mountains, past many auspicious rivers, they reached the sacred plateau of the Himālayas on the seventeenth day.

sanskrit: dadṛśuḥ pāṇḍavā rājan gandhamādanam antikāt pṛṣṭhe himavataḥ puṇye nānādrumalatāyute
english: The Pāṇḍavas, O king, saw Gandhamādana close at hand, on the sacred back of the Himālayas, covered with many trees and creepers.

sanskrit: salilāvartasaṃjātaiḥ puṣpitaiś ca mahīruhaiḥ samāvṛtaṃ puṇyatamam āśramaṃ vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ
english: Adorned with blooming great trees born from water-eddies, they saw the most sacred hermitage of Vṛṣaparvan.

sanskrit: tam upakramya rājarṣiṃ dharmātmānam ariṃdamāḥ pāṇḍavā vṛṣaparvāṇam avandanta gataklamāḥ
english: Approaching that royal sage Vṛṣaparvan, righteous-souled, the Pāṇḍavas, subduers of foes, free from fatigue, paid reverence to him.

sanskrit: abhyanandat sa rājarṣiḥ putravad bharatarṣabhān pūjitāś cāvasaṃs tatra saptarātram ariṃdamāḥ
english: That royal sage welcomed the bulls of the Bhārata race as a father would his sons; honored, those subduers of enemies dwelt there for seven nights.

sanskrit: aṣṭame 'hani saṃprāpte tam ṛṣiṃ lokaviśrutam āmantrya vṛṣaparvāṇaṃ prasthānaṃ samarocayan
english: When the eighth day arrived, they took leave of that sage famed throughout the world, Vṛṣaparvan, and resolved to depart.

sanskrit: ekaikaśaś ca tān viprān nivedya vṛṣaparvaṇe nyāsabhūtān yathākālaṃ bandhūn iva susatkṛtān
english: And presenting each of those brahmins one by one to Vṛṣaparvan, like treasured friends duly honoured, at the proper time,

sanskrit: tatas te varavastrāṇi śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca nyadadhuḥ pāṇḍavās tasminn āśrame vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ
english: then the Pāṇḍavas left behind their excellent garments and auspicious ornaments in that hermitage of Vṛṣaparvan.

sanskrit: atītānāgate vidvān kuśalaḥ sarvadharmavit anvaśāsat sa dharmajñaḥ putravad bharatarṣabhān
english: That wise one, skilled in past and future, knower of all dharma, that knower of righteousness, instructed the bulls of the Bhārata race as a father would his sons.

sanskrit: te 'nujñātā mahātmānaḥ prayayur diśam uttarām kṛṣṇayā sahitā vīrā brāhmaṇaiś ca mahātmabhiḥ tān prasthitān anvagacchad vṛṣaparvā mahīpatiḥ
english: Those great-souled heroes, given leave, journeyed northward together with Kṛṣṇā and great-souled brahmins; and Vṛṣaparvan, lord of the earth, followed them as they set out.

sanskrit: upanyasya mahātejā viprebhyaḥ pāṇḍavāṃs tadā anusaṃsādhya kaunteyān āśīrbhir abhinandya ca vṛṣaparvā nivavṛte panthānam upadiśya ca
english: The great-splendoured Vṛṣaparvan commended the Pāṇḍavas to the brahmins, blessed the sons of Kuntī with benedictions, congratulated them, and after showing them the path, turned back.

sanskrit: nānāmṛgagaṇair juṣṭaṃ kaunteyaḥ satyavikramaḥ padātir bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ prātiṣṭhata yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, of true valour, set out on foot together with his brothers through forests filled with many herds of animals.

sanskrit: nānādrumanirodheṣu vasantaḥ śailasānuṣu parvataṃ viviśuḥ śvetaṃ caturthe 'hani pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Dwelling on the mountain slopes amid many thickets of trees, the Pāṇḍavas entered Mount Śveta on the fourth day.

sanskrit: mahābhraghanasaṃkāśaṃ salilopahitaṃ śubham maṇikāñcanaramyaṃ ca śailaṃ nānāsamucchrayam
english: That mountain resembling a mass of great clouds, adorned with water, auspicious, beautiful with gems and gold, with its many soaring peaks.

sanskrit: te samāsādya panthānaṃ yathoktaṃ vṛṣaparvaṇā anusasrur yathoddeśaṃ paśyanto vividhān nagān
english: They reached the path as described by Vṛṣaparvan and followed it to its destination, beholding diverse mountains.

sanskrit: upary upari śailasya guhāḥ paramadurgamāḥ sudurgamāṃs te subahūn sukhenaivābhicakramuḥ
english: Going ever higher on the mountain, those very many most impassable, utterly inaccessible caves they traversed with ease.

sanskrit: dhaumyaḥ kṛṣṇā ca pārthāś ca lomaśaś ca mahān ṛṣiḥ agaman sahitās tatra na kaś cid avahīyate
english: Dhaumya, Kṛṣṇā, the Pārthas, and the great sage Lomaśa all went together there; not one fell behind.

sanskrit: te mṛgadvijasaṃghuṣṭaṃ nānādvijasamākulam śākhāmṛgagaṇaiś caiva sevitaṃ sumanoharam
english: That place resounded with animals and birds, teeming with many kinds of birds, frequented by troops of monkeys, and exceedingly beautiful.

sanskrit: puṇyaṃ padmasaropetaṃ sapalvalamahāvanam upatasthur mahāvīryā mālyavantaṃ mahāgirim
english: Those of great might approached the great mountain Mālyavān, sacred, with its lotus lakes, its great forest full of ponds.

sanskrit: tataḥ kiṃpuruṣāvāsaṃ siddhacāraṇasevitam dadṛśur hṛṣṭaromāṇaḥ parvataṃ gandhamādanam
english: Then with hairs standing on end in delight they saw the mountain Gandhamādana, abode of the Kiṃpuruṣas, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: vidyādharānucaritaṃ kiṃnarībhis tathaiva ca gajasiṃhasamākīrṇam udīrṇaśarabhāyutam
english: Attended by Vidyādharas and Kinnaras, it was dense with elephants and lions and filled with rampaging sharabhas.

sanskrit: upetam anyaiś ca tadā mṛgair mṛduninādibhiḥ te gandhamādanavanaṃ tan nandanavanopamam
english: Adorned then with other deer that called in gentle tones, that forest of Gandhamādana resembled Nandana, the divine grove.

sanskrit: muditāḥ pāṇḍutanayā manohṛdayanandanam viviśuḥ kramaśo vīrā araṇyaṃ śubhakānanam
english: Joyful, the sons of Pāṇḍu, those heroes, entered step by step that forest, heart-gladdening and auspicious.

sanskrit: draupadīsahitā vīrās taiś ca viprair mahātmabhiḥ śṛṇvantaḥ prītijananān valgūn madakalāñ śubhān śrotraramyān sumadhurāñ śabdān khagamukheritān
english: Those heroes together with Draupadī and those great-souled brahmins, listening to gladsome, sweet, intoxicating, auspicious, ear-delighting, melodious sounds uttered from the mouths of birds,

sanskrit: sarvartuphalabhārāḍhyān sarvartukusumojjvalān paśyantaḥ pādapāṃś cāpi phalabhārāvanāmitān
english: beholding trees laden with fruit of every season, blazing with blossoms of every season, and bowing down under their burden of fruit,

sanskrit: āmrān āmrātakān phullān nārikelān satindukān ajātakāṃs tathā jīrān dāḍimān bījapūrakān
english: mangoes, blooming amrataka, coconuts, ebony trees, ajataka, jira trees, pomegranates, and citrons,

sanskrit: panasāṃl likucān mocān kharjūrān āmravetasān pārāvatāṃs tathā kṣaudrān nīpāṃś cāpi manoramān
english: jackfruit, licucha, banana, date palms, mango-cane, pāravata trees, sweet-honey trees, and charming nipa trees,

sanskrit: bilvān kapitthāñ jambūṃś ca kāśmarīr badarīs tathā plakṣān udumbaravaṭān aśvatthān kṣīriṇas tathā bhallātakān āmalakān harītakabibhītakān
english: bel trees, wood-apples, rose-apple trees, kashmari, jujube, plaksha, udumbara, banyan, peepal, and milky trees, marking-nut trees, emblic myrobalan, chebulic and belleric myrobalan,

sanskrit: iṅgudān karavīrāṃś ca tindukāṃś ca mahāphalān etān anyāṃś ca vividhān gandhamādanasānuṣu
english: inguda, oleander, and tinduka bearing large fruits — these and other diverse trees on the slopes of Gandhamādana,

sanskrit: phalair amṛtakalpais tān ācitān svādubhis tarūn tathaiva campakāśokān ketakān bakulāṃs tathā
english: those trees laden with sweet, nectar-like fruits, and likewise champaka, ashoka, ketaka, and bakula trees,

sanskrit: puṃnāgān saptaparṇāṃś ca karṇikārān saketakān pāṭalān kuṭajān ramyān mandārendīvarāṃs tathā
english: pumnaga, saptaparna, karnikara, saketaka, patala, charming kutaja, mandara, and indivara lotuses,

sanskrit: pārijātān kovidārān devadārutarūṃs tathā śālāṃs tālāṃs tamālāṃś ca priyālān bakulāṃs tathā śālmalīḥ kiṃśukāśokāñ śiṃśapāṃs taralāṃs tathā
english: parijata, kovidara, and deodar trees, shala, palmyra, tamala, priyal, bakula, silk-cotton trees, flame of the forest, ashoka, simsapa, and tarala trees,

sanskrit: cakoraiḥ śatapatraiś ca bhṛṅgarājais tathā śukaiḥ kokilaiḥ kalaviṅkaiś ca hārītair jīvajīvakaiḥ
english: frequented by cakora birds, shanapatra birds, bhringarajas, parrots, cuckoos, sparrows, harita birds, and chakravaka birds,

sanskrit: priyavrataiś cātakaiś ca tathānyair vividhaiḥ khagaiḥ śrotraramyaṃ sumadhuraṃ kūjadbhiś cāpy adhiṣṭhitān
english: by chataka birds of pleasant ways and other varied birds cooing ear-delightingly sweet — they beheld those trees.

sanskrit: sarāṃsi ca vicitrāṇi prasannasalilāni ca kumudaiḥ puṇḍarīkaiś ca tathā kokanadotpalaiḥ kahlāraiḥ kamalaiś caiva ācitāni samantataḥ
english: And beautiful lakes with clear water, covered on all sides with white water-lilies, lotuses, red and blue lotuses, water-lilies, and kamala lotuses.

sanskrit: kadambaiś cakravākaiś ca kurarair jalakukkuṭaiḥ kāraṇḍavaiḥ plavair haṃsair bakair madgubhir eva ca etaiś cānyaiś ca kīrṇāni samantāj jalacāribhiḥ
english: Filled on all sides with kadamba ducks, chakravaka geese, kurara birds, water hens, karandava ducks, divers, swans, herons, and cormorants — these and other water-birds.

sanskrit: hṛṣṭais tathā tāmarasarasāsavamadālasaiḥ padmodaracyutarajaḥkiñjalkāruṇarañjitaiḥ
english: And those joyful birds, languid with the nectar-wine of lotus ponds, tinted red with pollen and filaments fallen from the hearts of lotuses,

sanskrit: madhurasvarair madhukarair virutān kamalākarān paśyantas te manoramyān gandhamādanasānuṣu
english: they beheld those charming lotus-groves on the slopes of Gandhamādana, humming with sweet-voiced bees.

sanskrit: tathaiva padmaṣaṇḍaiś ca maṇḍiteṣu samantataḥ śikhaṇḍinībhiḥ sahitāṃl latāmaṇḍapakeṣu ca meghatūryaravoddāmamadanākulitān bhṛśam
english: And likewise in the bower-pavilions of creepers adorned on all sides with clusters of lotuses, in company with their peahens, they saw peacocks greatly agitated by passion stirred by the roar of clouds like trumpets.

sanskrit: kṛtvaiva kekāmadhuraṃ saṃgītamadhurasvaram citrān kalāpān vistīrya savilāsān madālasān mayūrān dadṛśuś citrān nṛtyato vanalāsakān
english: Having uttered sweet peacock-cries and sweet singing sounds, spreading their lovely tail-feathers with grace and languor — they saw those beautiful peacocks dancing in forest play.

sanskrit: kāntābhiḥ sahitān anyān apaśyan ramataḥ sukham vallīlatāsaṃkaṭeṣu kaṭakeṣu sthitāṃs tathā
english: They saw others sporting happily with their mates, dwelling in the thickets of creepers and in bracelets of clinging vines.

sanskrit: kāṃś cic chakunajātāṃś ca viṭapeṣūtkaṭān api kalāparacitāṭopān vicitramukuṭān iva vivareṣu tarūṇāṃ ca muditān dadṛśuś ca te
english: They also saw certain kinds of birds, preening in the tree-branches, their displays arranged with tail-feathers, as if wearing wonderful crowns, and they were seen in the hollows of trees, delighted.

sanskrit: sindhuvārān athoddāmān manmathasyeva tomarān suvarṇakusumākīrṇān girīṇāṃ śikhareṣu ca
english: And the sindhuvara plants, unbridled, like darts of the God of Love, scattered with golden flowers on the peaks of mountains,

sanskrit: karṇikārān viracitān karṇapūrān ivottamān athāpaśyan kurabakān vanarājiṣu puṣpitān kāmavaśyotsukakarān kāmasyeva śarotkarān
english: the karnikara trees beautifully formed like exquisite ear-ornaments — they then saw kurabaka bushes in bloom in the forest rows, arousing eager desire as if they were love's own arrows.

sanskrit: tathaiva vanarājīnām udārān racitān iva virājamānāṃs te 'paśyaṃs tilakāṃs tilakān iva
english: Similarly in the forest rows they saw tilaka trees, noble, as if arranged, blazing like the tilaka mark itself.

sanskrit: tathānaṅgaśarākārān sahakārān manoramān apaśyan bhramarārāvān mañjarībhir virājitān
english: They saw likewise charming sahakara trees shaped like the shafts of the bodiless God of Love, resplendent with clusters of blossoms amid the hum of bees.

sanskrit: hiraṇyasadṛśaiḥ puṣpair dāvāgnisadṛśair api lohitair añjanābhaiś ca vaiḍūryasadṛśair api
english: With flowers resembling gold and others resembling forest fire, and with crimson ones and blue-black ones and yet others resembling beryl,

sanskrit: tathā śālāṃs tamālāṃś ca pāṭalyo bakulāni ca mālā iva samāsaktāḥ śailānāṃ śikhareṣu ca
english: and shala, tamala, patali, and bakula trees hanging together like garlands on the peaks of mountains —

sanskrit: evaṃ krameṇa te vīrā vīkṣamāṇāḥ samantataḥ gajasaṃghasamābādhaṃ siṃhavyāghrasamāyutam
english: Thus step by step those heroes, gazing all around at those slopes of Gandhamādana crowded with herds of elephants, filled with lions and tigers,

sanskrit: śarabhonnādasaṃghuṣṭaṃ nānārāvanināditam sarvartuphalapuṣpāḍhyaṃ gandhamādanasānuṣu
english: resounding with the cries of sharabhas, echoing with varied roars, rich with fruits and flowers of all seasons —

sanskrit: pītā bhāsvaravarṇābhā babhūvur vanarājayaḥ nātra kaṇṭakinaḥ ke cin nātra ke cid apuṣpitāḥ snigdhapatraphalā vṛkṣā gandhamādanasānuṣu
english: the rows of trees became yellow-gleaming and radiant in hue; here were no thorny trees, here none without flowers; the trees on the slopes of Gandhamādana had glossy leaves and fruits.

sanskrit: vimalasphaṭikābhāni pāṇḍuracchadanair dvijaiḥ rājahaṃsair upetāni sārasābhirutāni ca sarāṃsi saritaḥ pārthāḥ paśyantaḥ śailasānuṣu
english: The Pārthas beheld on the mountain slopes lakes and rivers clear as crystal, visited by white-winged birds and royal swans, resounding with the cries of cranes.

sanskrit: padmotpalavicitrāṇi sukhasparśajalāni ca gandhavanti ca mālyāni rasavanti phalāni ca atīva vṛkṣā rājante puṣpitāḥ śailasānuṣu
english: Beautiful with lotuses and blue lilies, with pleasantly cool water, fragrant garlands, juicy fruits — exceedingly splendid were the blossoming trees on the mountain slopes.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavas tatra kānanajā drumāḥ latāś ca vividhākārāḥ patrapuṣpaphaloccayāḥ
english: These and many others were the forest-born trees there, and creepers of diverse shapes, laden with leaves, flowers, and fruits.
